claim: RESOLFT nanoscopy requires relatively low light levels to overcome the diffraction barrier.
source: RESOLFT nanoscopy is particularly suited for live cell imaging because it requires relatively low light levels to overcome the diffraction barrier.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a characteristic of RESOLFT nanoscopy.

claim: rsEGFP2 was previously introduced as a reversibly switchable fluorescent protein that facilitated fast RESOLFT nanoscopy.
source: Previously, we introduced the reversibly switchable fluorescent protein rsEGFP2, which facilitated fast RESOLFT nanoscopy (Grotjohann et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Grotjohann et al., 2012).

claim: The study generated flies expressing fusion proteins of alpha-tubulin and rsEGFP2 highlighting the microtubule cytoskeleton in all cells.
source: We generated flies expressing fusion proteins of alpha-tubulin and rsEGFP2 highlighting the microtubule cytoskeleton in all cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of what was done in the study.

claim: By focusing through the intact larval cuticle, lateral resolution of <60 nm was achieved.
source: By focusing through the intact larval cuticle, we achieved lateral resolution of <60 nm.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the resolution achieved, supported by experimental data.

claim: RESOLFT nanoscopy enabled time-lapse recordings comprising 40 images.
source: RESOLFT nanoscopy enabled time-lapse recordings comprising 40 images and facilitated recordings 40 µm deep within fly tissues.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental capability demonstrated in the study.

claim: RESOLFT nanoscopy facilitated recordings 40 µm deep within fly tissues.
source: RESOLFT nanoscopy enabled time-lapse recordings comprising 40 images and facilitated recordings 40 µm deep within fly tissues.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental capability demonstrated in the study.

claim: Nanoscopy of thick specimen is mostly performed on optically transparent samples such as cleared and fixed tissue.
source: Indeed, nanoscopy of thick specimen is mostly performed on optically transparent samples such as cleared and fixed tissue (Stelzer, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Stelzer, 2015.

claim: The relatively few reported examples of nanoscopy in living tissues typically relied on specimen in which individual cells overexpressed a fluorescent protein.
source: The relatively few reported examples of nanoscopy in living tissues typically relied on specimen in which individual cells overexpressed a fluorescent protein (Nägerl et al., 2008; Chéreau et al., 2015; Berning et al., 2012; Yuste and Bonhoeffer, 2004; Testa et al., 2012; Tønnesen et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: rsEGFP2 is a very photostable reversibly switchable fluorescent protein.
source: To overcome this shortcoming, we previously reported the generation of rsEGFP2 (Grotjohann et al., 2012), a very photostable reversibly switchable fluorescent protein (RSFP).
evidence: This is a direct characterization of rsEGFP2 with citation support.

claim: The green fluorescent rsEGFP2 can be reversibly photo-switched between a fluorescent 'On-' and a non-fluorescent 'Off-'state with light of ~405 nm and ~488 nm.
source: The green fluorescent rsEGFP2 can be reversible photo-switched between a fluorescent 'On-' and a non-fluorescent 'Off-'state with light of ~405 nm and ~488 nm.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the optical properties of rsEGFP2.

claim: rsEGFP2 was designed to be used within the framework of live-cell RESOLFT nanoscopy.
source: rsEGFP2 was designed to be used within the framework of live-cell RESOLFT (reversible saturable optical fluorescence transition) nanoscopy (Hell et al., 2004; Brakemann et al., 2011; Grotjohann et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the design purpose of rsEGFP2, supported by citations.

claim: In its initial application, rsEGFP2 was only used to study sub-cellular dynamics in single-layered cultivated cells.
source: In its initial application, however, rsEGFP2 was only used to study sub-cellular dynamics in single-layered cultivated cells (Grotjohann et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the initial application study.

claim: The light intensities used in RESOLFT are up to six orders of magnitude lower than those in STED-microscopy.
source: The light intensities used are up to six orders of magnitude lower than those in STED-microscopy (Klar et al., 2000) and are comparable to those typically applied in live-cell confocal fluorescence microscopy (Wäldchen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a direct comparison statement supported by citations.

claim: The light intensities used in RESOLFT are comparable to those typically applied in live-cell confocal fluorescence microscopy.
source: The light intensities used are up to six orders of magnitude lower than those in STED-microscopy (Klar et al., 2000) and are comparable to those typically applied in live-cell confocal fluorescence microscopy (Wäldchen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a direct comparison statement supported by citations.

claim: The total light dose impinging on the sample in RESOLFT is lower by 3–4 orders of magnitude compared to stochastic single-molecule based nanoscopy approaches.
source: Likewise, the total light dose impinging on the sample is lower by 3–4 orders of magnitude compared to stochastic single-molecule based nanoscopy approaches (Grotjohann et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a direct comparison statement supported by a citation.

claim: RESOLFT can be combined with confocal detection when implemented in a beam scanning approach.
source: Furthermore, when implemented in a beam scanning approach, RESOLFT can be combined with confocal detection, which is particularly suitable for the imaging of highly fluorescent tissues because it rejects the out-of-focus fluorescence.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the technical capabilities of RESOLFT.

claim: Confocal detection is particularly suitable for the imaging of highly fluorescent tissues because it rejects the out-of-focus fluorescence.
source: Furthermore, when implemented in a beam scanning approach, RESOLFT can be combined with confocal detection, which is particularly suitable for the imaging of highly fluorescent tissues because it rejects the out-of-focus fluorescence.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the advantage of confocal detection.

claim: RESOLFT microscopy is particularly suitable for live-cell imaging of complex samples such as tissues.
source: Altogether, this suggests that RESOLFT microscopy is particularly suitable for live-cell imaging of complex samples such as tissues.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the preceding technical characteristics.

claim: Neither RESOLFT nor any other diffraction-unlimited super-resolution microscopy approach has so far been used to image subcellular details in living transgenic animals ubiquitously expressing a fusion protein.
source: Still, to our knowledge, neither RESOLFT nor any other diffraction-unlimited super-resolution microscopy approach has so far been used to image subcellular details in living transgenic animals ubiquitously expressing a fusion protein.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to this study.

claim: The study demonstrates live-cell RESOLFT nanoscopy on living transgenic fly tissues and intact larvae whose microtubule network was labelled in all cells by ubiquitously expressing rsEGFP2 fused to α-tubulin.
source: In this study we demonstrate live-cell RESOLFT nanoscopy on living transgenic fly tissues and intact larvae whose microtubule network was labelled in all cells by ubiquitously expressing rsEGFP2 fused to α-tubulin.
evidence: This is a direct statement of what was demonstrated in the study.

claim: Flies expressing rsEGFP2-α-tubulin were generated under the transcriptional control of the ubiquitin 68E promotor ensuring moderate expression levels of the fusion protein.
source: In order to enable RESOLFT nanoscopy of living Drosophila melanogaster, we generated flies expressing rsEGFP2-α-tubulin ubiquitously under the transcriptional control of the ubiquitin 68E promotor ensuring moderate expression levels of the fusion protein.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental approach.

claim: Confocal images of resected tissues from transgenic adult flies revealed a large variation of the arrangement of the microtubule cytoskeleton depending on the cell type.
source: Confocal images of resected tissues from transgenic adult flies revealed a large variation of the arrangement of the microtubule cytoskeleton depending on the cell type (Figure 1A–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by confocal imaging data shown in Figure 1.

claim: At 25°C, the half-time of the life span of transgenic flies expressing rsEGFP2-α-tubulin was ~41 days, similar to the isogenic wild type strain.
source: At 25°C, the half-time of the life span of these flies was ~41 days, similar to the isogenic wild type strain.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observation comparing transgenic and wild-type flies.

claim: The transgenic flies were propagated for more than 50 generations without detecting any loss in fitness.
source: The flies were propagated for more than 50 generations without detecting any loss in fitness.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observation.

claim: During oogenesis and spermatogenesis the microtubule network was labelled in transgenic flies expressing rsEGFP2-α-tubulin.
source: The fact that even during oogenesis and spermatogenesis the microtubule network was labelled (Figure 1D,E) suggests no adverse effects of the ubiquitous expression of rsEGFP2-α-tubulin on the embryogenesis and demonstrates the versatility of rsEGFP2 as a live-cell label.
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1D,E.

claim: The labelling of the microtubule network during oogenesis and spermatogenesis suggests no adverse effects of the ubiquitous expression of rsEGFP2-α-tubulin on the embryogenesis.
source: The fact that even during oogenesis and spermatogenesis the microtubule network was labelled (Figure 1D,E) suggests no adverse effects of the ubiquitous expression of rsEGFP2-α-tubulin on the embryogenesis and demonstrates the versatility of rsEGFP2 as a live-cell label.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that labelling occurs during these critical developmental stages.

claim: The labelling of the microtubule network during oogenesis and spermatogenesis demonstrates the versatility of rsEGFP2 as a live-cell label.
source: The fact that even during oogenesis and spermatogenesis the microtubule network was labelled (Figure 1D,E) suggests no adverse effects of the ubiquitous expression of rsEGFP2-α-tubulin on the embryogenesis and demonstrates the versatility of rsEGFP2 as a live-cell label.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that labelling occurs during these critical developmental stages.

claim: Western blots of larval protein extracts probed with antiserum against α-tubulin demonstrated that the fusion protein was expressed at moderate levels, so that the ratio of endogenous α-tubulin to rsEGFP2-α-tubulin was about 3:1.
source: Western blots of larval protein extracts probed with antiserum against α-tubulin demonstrated that the fusion protein was expressed at moderate levels, so that the ratio of endogenous α-tubulin to rsEGFP2-α-tubulin was about 3:1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: A stable transgenic fly line ubiquitously expressing rsEGFP2-α-tubulin in all tissues specifically highlighting the microtubule cytoskeleton without interfering with the fly fitness was generated.
source: Together, we generated a stable transgenic fly line ubiquitously expressing rsEGFP2-α-tubulin in all tissues specifically highlighting the microtubule cytoskeleton without interfering with the fly fitness.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental results.

claim: RESOLFT images of various tissues including body wall muscles and salivary glands were recorded, demonstrating a distinct improvement in resolution compared to the corresponding confocal images.
source: We recorded RESOLFT images of various tissues including body wall muscles (Figure 2A–C) and salivary glands (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), demonstrating a distinct improvement in resolution compared to the corresponding confocal images.
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The increased resolution in RESOLFT imaging is well exemplified in body wall muscle cells, where microtubules are frequently co-aligned over relatively long distances.
source: The increased resolution is well exemplified in body wall muscle cells, where microtubules are frequently co-aligned over relatively long distances (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2B,C.

claim: The FWHM values of rsEGFP2-α-tubulin labeled microtubules in RESOLFT images were consistently around 50–60 nm.
source: The FWHM values were consistently around 50–60 nm (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B; Figure 3—figure supplement 1), which represents an ~4-fold improvement over the diffraction limited resolution.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The FWHM values of 50–60 nm represent an ~4-fold improvement over the diffraction limited resolution.
source: The FWHM values were consistently around 50–60 nm (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B; Figure 3—figure supplement 1), which represents an ~4-fold improvement over the diffraction limited resolution.
evidence: This is a direct comparison of RESOLFT resolution to diffraction-limited resolution.

claim: 14 RESOLFT images of resected body wall muscle tissue with 250 nm axial distance between each image were recorded to track individual microtubules in the tissue volume.
source: To make use of this property, we recorded 14 RESOLFT images of resected body wall muscle tissue with 250 nm axial distance between each image. Thereby one can track individual microtubules in the tissue volume (Figure 2—figure supplement 2; Video 1), albeit at relatively poor axial resolution.
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and Video 1.

claim: The 2D-doughnut was replaced by a 3D-doughnut to increase the resolution along the x,y, and z-axes.
source: In order to track the microtubules more reliably in 3D, we replaced the 2D-doughnut by a 3D-doughnut, which confines the On-state rsEGFP2 molcules in all room directions, thus increasing the resolution along the x,y, and z-axes.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the technical modification made.

claim: Using the 3D-doughnut, 33 RESOLFT images in a 2 µm thick volume element with an ~4 fold improved axial resolution were imaged.
source: Using this we imaged 33 RESOLFT images in a 2 µm thick volume element with an ~4 fold improved axial resolution (Figure 2—figure supplement 3; Video 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and Video 2.

claim: RESOLFT nanoscopy facilitates sub-diffraction imaging in living resected tissues to visualize structures not accessible by conventional microscopy.
source: We conclude that RESOLFT nanoscopy facilitates sub-diffraction imaging in living resected tissues to visualize structures not accessible by conventional microscopy.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Confocal images exhibited reduced signal-to-noise ratios already at an imaging depth of 10 µm due to the pronounced scattering in the tissue.
source: Still, the confocal images exhibited reduced signal-to-noise ratios already at an imaging depth of 10 µm due to the pronounced scattering in the tissue.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observation.

claim: At an imaging depth of 42 µm the rsEGFP2-α-tubulin labeled microtubules were barely discernible when imaged in the confocal mode.
source: This undesirable effect strengthened with increasing imaging depths such that at an imaging depth of 42 µm the rsEGFP2-α-tubulin labeled microtubules were barely discernible when imaged in the confocal mode (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Using RESOLFT nanoscopy, the highest attainable resolution and the best signal-to-noise ratio were recorded in the top layer of the opened larvae.
source: Using RESOLFT nanoscopy, the highest attainable resolution and the best signal-to-noise ratio were recorded in the top layer of the opened larvae (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: At deeper cell layers, RESOLFT resolved individual microtubule filaments with a substantially better signal-to-noise ratio than in the confocal case.
source: However, also at deeper cell layers, we resolved individual microtubule filaments with a substantially better signal-to-noise ratio than in the confocal case.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observation.

claim: The advantage of RESOLFT is attributed to the beneficial effect of transferring the rsEGFP2 molecules outside of the focus to a non-fluorescent state before probing the fluorescence, thus improving the contrast.
source: We attribute this advantage of RESOLFT to the beneficial effect of transferring the rsEGFP2 molecules outside of the focus to a non-fluorescent state before probing the fluorescence, thus improving the contrast.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism underlying the observed advantage.

claim: The resolution in RESOLFT decreased with the penetration depth, but was always better than in the corresponding confocal images.
source: The resolution decreased with the penetration depth, but was always better than in the corresponding confocal images.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observation.

claim: The RESOLFT mode allows retrieving image information deep within scattering and highly fluorescent tissue that is inaccessible by confocal microscopy.
source: Hence the RESOLFT mode allows retrieving image information deep within scattering and highly fluorescent tissue that is inaccessible by confocal microscopy.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Living intact Drosophila larvae are difficult samples for fluorescence microscopy because of their challenging optical properties, frequent irregular movements, and the cuticle induced light scattering.
source: Living intact Drosophila larvae are difficult samples for fluorescence microscopy, not only because of their challenging optical properties, but also because of their frequent irregular movements and the cuticle induced light scattering.
evidence: This is a statement about the challenges of imaging intact larvae.

claim: In samples that express the fusion proteins in all cells, very pronounced out-of-focus fluorescence may occur.
source: Moreover, in samples that express the fusion proteins in all cells, very pronounced out-of-focus fluorescence may occur.
evidence: This is a statement about a potential imaging challenge.

claim: Living rsEGFP2-α-tubulin expressing second instar larvae were placed between two spacers that separated the object slide and the cover glass, forming a cavity filled with Schneider's cell culture media.
source: To enable RESOLFT microscopy in intact larvae, living rsEGFP2-α-tubulin expressing second instar larvae were placed between two spacers that separated the object slide and the cover glass, forming a cavity filled with Schneider's cell culture media (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental method, illustrated in Figure 3A.

claim: The overall movements of the larvae were largely restrained by the spacer setup, although movements of body muscles still occurred.
source: By this, the overall movements of the larvae were largely restrained, although movements of body muscles still occurred.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observation.

claim: For RESOLFT imaging, the microscope was focused through the intact larval cuticle into the underlying tissue without any further treatment of the larvae.
source: For RESOLFT imaging, we focused through the intact larval cuticle into the underlying tissue without any further treatment of the larvae.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental approach.

claim: Despite the occasional movements of the larvae, RESOLFT images of the microtubule network in intact animals could be reliably recorded.
source: Despite the occasional movements of the larvae, we could reliably record RESOLFT images of the microtubule network in these intact animals.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observation.

claim: Co-aligned microtubules that were fully blurred in the corresponding confocal images could be resolved in RESOLFT images of intact larvae.
source: Co-aligned microtubules that were fully blurred in the corresponding confocal images could be resolved (Figure 3B–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3B–D.

claim: The measured resolution in the intact larvae was also ≤60 nm, despite the fact that imaging was done through the opaque cuticle into tissue.
source: As in resected tissues, the measured resolution in the intact larvae was also ≤60 nm (Figure 3E; Figure 3—figure supplement 1), despite the fact that we were focusing through the opaque cuticle into tissue.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 3E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: RESOLFT imaging is feasible even on living larvae expressing rsEGFP2-fusion proteins without removing the cuticle and thus leaving the larvae entirely intact.
source: We conclude that RESOLFT imaging is feasible even on living larvae expressing rsEGFP2-fusion proteins without removing the cuticle and thus leaving the larvae entirely intact.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Over a large field of view of 552 µm2, dissected larval body wall muscles were imaged continuously for 2.5 hr in the RESOLFT mode, thereby recording 40 RESOLFT images.
source: Over a large field of view of 552 µm2, we imaged dissected larval body wall muscles continuously for 2.5 hr in the RESOLFT mode, thereby recording 40 RESOLFT images (Figure 4A, Video 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4A and Video 3.

claim: At the end of the 2.5 hr recording, the microtubules still displayed alternating periods of growth and shrinkage.
source: At the end of the recording, the microtubules still displayed alternating periods of growth and shrinkage.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observation.

claim: During the extended imaging period no obvious signs of cellular distress were observed, neither in the recorded area nor in the surrounding cells, despite recognizable photobleaching.
source: During this extended imaging period we observed no obvious signs of cellular distress, neither in the recorded area nor in the surrounding cells, despite recognizable photobleaching (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observation, with supporting data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: To follow the growth and depolymerization of individual microtubules, the field of view was reduced to 52 µm2 and the imaging conditions were adapted to record a single RESOLFT image in 9.3 s.
source: To follow the growth and depolymerization of individual microtubules, we reduced the field of view to 52 µm2 and adapted the imaging conditions to record a single RESOLFT image in 9.3 s (Figure 4B, Video 4).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental approach, with supporting data in Figure 4B and Video 4.

claim: At a frame rate of 9.3 s per image, 40 RESOLFT images were recorded, facilitating the tracking of microtubule dynamics.
source: At this frame rate we recorded 40 RESOLFT images, facilitating the tracking of microtubule dynamics.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observation.

claim: RESOLFT microscopy can be utilized for time-lapse recordings of dynamic sub-cellular processes in highly fluorescent tissues.
source: Hence RESOLFT microscopy can be utilized for time-lapse recordings of dynamic sub-cellular processes in highly fluorescent tissues.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: In previous RESOLFT studies, live cell recordings of only single cells were reported.
source: In previous RESOLFT studies, live cell recordings of only single cells were reported (Tiwari et al., 2015, Duwé et al., 2015; El Khatib et al., 2016; Brakemann et al., 2011; Grotjohann et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: The use of rsEGFP2 was extended to in vivo RESOLFT imaging of tissues and larvae.
source: We extended the use of rsEGFP2 (Grotjohann et al., 2012) to in vivo RESOLFT imaging of tissues and larvae.
evidence: This is a direct statement of what was accomplished in the study.

claim: No detrimental effects of the ubiquitous expression of rsEGFP2-α-tubulin fusion proteins to the flies were observed during this study.
source: During this study we did not observe detrimental effects of the ubiquitous expression of rsEGFP2-α-tubulin fusion proteins to the flies.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observation.

claim: No phototoxic effects during imaging were observed.
source: Importantly, we also did not observe phototoxic effects during imaging.
evidence: This is a direct statement of experimental observation.

claim: The lack of phototoxic effects is attributed to the relatively low light intensities required in RESOLFT nanoscopy to overcome the diffraction barrier.
source: We attribute this to the relatively low light intensities required in RESOLFT nanoscopy to overcome the diffraction barrier.
evidence: This is an inference about the reason for the lack of phototoxicity.

claim: Because of the utilized scanning approach, the individual irradiation times are short and consequently the overall light dose deposited in the imaged volume is small.
source: Moreover, because of the utilized scanning approach, the individual irradiation times are short and consequently the overall light dose deposited in the imaged volume is small.
evidence: This is a statement about the technical characteristics of the scanning approach.

claim: The light intensities in RESOLFT microscopy are still higher than what is sometimes regarded as critical intensity threshold in long-term imaging to follow developmental processes over hours or even days.
source: Nonetheless, the light intensities in RESOLFT microscopy are still higher than what is sometimes regarded as critical intensity threshold in long-term imaging to follow developmental processes over hours or even days (Stelzer, 2015).
evidence: This is a statement comparing RESOLFT light intensities to those used in long-term imaging, supported by a citation.

claim: In in vivo RESOLFT microscopy, typically only a very small part of the sample organism is imaged, whereas the remaining parts are not illuminated.
source: It should be noted, however, that in in vivo RESOLFT microscopy, typically only a very small part of the sample organism is imaged, whereas the remaining parts are not illuminated.
evidence: This is a statement about the typical imaging approach in in vivo RESOLFT.

claim: The phototoxic effects that manifest themselves after the actual experiment are irrelevant as long as the cellular dynamics during the imaging are not disturbed.
source: Generally, the phototoxic effects that manifest themselves after the actual experiment are irrelevant as long as the cellular dynamics during the imaging are not disturbed.
evidence: This is a general statement about the relevance of phototoxicity in imaging experiments.

claim: The relatively low light intensities required for RESOLFT nanoscopy and the flexibility of the method offer additional freedom in the choice between resolution and recording time.
source: The relatively low light intensities required for RESOLFT nanoscopy and the flexibility of the method offer additional freedom in the choice between resolution and recording time: In RESOLFT nanoscopy, the attained resolution can be adjusted so that, for example, the resolution is decreased in favor of reduced phototoxicity, increased recording speed, or the number of images taken before bleaching.
evidence: This is a statement about the flexibility of RESOLFT nanoscopy.

claim: In RESOLFT nanoscopy, the attained resolution can be adjusted so that the resolution is decreased in favor of reduced phototoxicity, increased recording speed, or the number of images taken before bleaching.
source: In RESOLFT nanoscopy, the attained resolution can be adjusted so that, for example, the resolution is decreased in favor of reduced phototoxicity, increased recording speed, or the number of images taken before bleaching.
evidence: This is a statement about the flexibility of RESOLFT nanoscopy.

claim: The RESOLFT data could be deconvolved to increase the contrast and resolution even further if required.
source: Although in this manuscript we only show raw image data, the RESOLFT data could be deconvolved to increase the contrast and resolution even further if required.
evidence: This is a statement about potential post-processing of RESOLFT data.

claim: The RESOLFT modality offers the benefit of allowing to image deeper in tissue.
source: As shown here, the RESOLFT modality offers the benefit of allowing to image deeper in tissue.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The benefit of imaging deeper in tissue relies on the fact that fluorescence from outside the focal region is precluded because the molecules located in that region are transferred into a non-fluorescent state; their signal cannot perturb the image.
source: This observation relys on the fact that fluorescence from outside the focal region is precluded because the molecules located in that region are transferred into a non-fluorescent state; their signal cannot perturb the image.
evidence: This is an explanation of the mechanism underlying the benefit of RESOLFT for deep tissue imaging.

claim: Since the release of rsEGFP2 in 2012, a number of novel switchable fluorescent proteins have been reported.
source: Since the release of rsEGFP2 in 2012 (Grotjohann et al., 2012), a number of novel switchable fluorescent proteins have been reported.
evidence: This is a statement about developments in the field since 2012.

claim: rsFolder, rsGreen, rsEGFP-N205S, rsCherryRev1.4, and Kohinoor have been successfully used in RESOLFT nanoscopy.
source: Of these, the rsEGFP/rsEGFP2 variants rsFolder (El Khatib et al., 2016), rsGreen (Duwé et al., 2015), and rsEGFP-N205S (Chmyrov et al., 2013), the red fluorescent rsCherryRev1.4 (Lavoie-Cardinal et al., 2014), and the positive switching Kohinoor (Tiwari et al., 2015) have been successfully used in RESOLFT nanoscopy.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Organic dyes were used in RESOLFT nanoscopy.
source: Also organic dyes were used in this concept (Kwon et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: For the applications shown in this manuscript, namely beam scanning RESOLFT nanoscopy in tissues, rsEGFP2 seems to unite the necessary properties in the most suitable combination.
source: Still, for the applications shown in this manuscript, namely beam scanning RESOLFT nanoscopy in tissues, rsEGFP2 seems to unite the necessary properties in the most suitable combination.
evidence: This is an assessment of rsEGFP2 relative to other available fluorescent proteins for the specific application.

claim: rsEGFP2 dramatically outperforms earlier RSFPs such as Dronpa or rsEGFP.
source: Although rsEGFP2 dramatically outperforms earlier RSFPs such as Dronpa (Ando et al., 2004) or rsEGFP (Grotjohann et al., 2011), we expect generation of superior RSFPs in the future that are even more photostable, brighter, and exhibit better contrast.
evidence: This is a comparative statement supported by citations to prior work on Dronpa and rsEGFP.

claim: Superior RSFPs that are even more photostable, brighter, and exhibit better contrast are expected to be generated in the future.
source: Although rsEGFP2 dramatically outperforms earlier RSFPs such as Dronpa (Ando et al., 2004) or rsEGFP (Grotjohann et al., 2011), we expect generation of superior RSFPs in the future that are even more photostable, brighter, and exhibit better contrast.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future developments.

claim: With the ongoing developments both on RSFPs as well as on instrumentation, it can be anticipated that the application range of low light RESOLFT nanoscopy in Drosophila as well as in other multicellular organism will be further expanded in the future.
source: We conclude that with the ongoing developments both on RSFPs as well as on instrumentation, it can be anticipated that the application range of low light RESOLFT nanoscopy in Drosophila as well as in other multicellular organism will be further expanded in the future.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future applications.

claim: A synthetic gene sequence encoding the fluorescent protein rsEGFP2 attached to the N-terminus of the α-tubulin 84B protein was synthesized.
source: A synthetic gene sequence encoding the fluorescent protein rsEGFP2 (GenBank #AGE84598.1) attached to the N-terminus of the α-tubulin 84B (cg1913, UniProt #P06603) protein was synthesized.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the cloning approach.

claim: The DNA was cloned into an attB-containing fly transformation vector under the control of the Ubiquitin p63E promotor-region.
source: The DNA was cloned into an attB-containing fly transformation vector under the control of the Ubiquitin p63E promotor-region (3L; 3901762 to 3903743).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the cloning approach.

claim: To generate transgenic flies, a standard phiC31 integrase based germ line transformation procedure was followed, targeting the landing site M{3xP3-RFP.attP}ZH-86Fb using Bloomington stock #24749.
source: To generate transgenic flies, a standard phiC31 integrase based germ line transformation procedure was followed, targeting the landing site M{3xP3-RFP.attP}ZH-86Fb using Bloomington stock #24749 (Bischof et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the method used to generate transgenic flies, supported by a citation.

claim: RESOLFT nanoscopy was performed using a modified 1C RESOLFT QUAD Scanning microscope.
source: RESOLFT nanoscopy was performed using a modified 1C RESOLFT QUAD Scanning microscope (Abberior Instruments, Goettingen, Germany).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the instrumentation used.

claim: For RESOLFT imaging of Drosophila melanogaster, rsEGFP2 proteins were first switched into the on-state with light of 405 nm.
source: For RESOLFT imaging of Drosophila melanogaster, the following switching scheme was applied to the sample at each scanning position: First, rsEGFP2 proteins were switched into the on-state with light of 405 nm.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the imaging protocol.

claim: rsEGFP2 proteins in the periphery of the focal spot were switched off using a 488 nm doughnut-shaped beam.
source: Second, rsEGFP2 proteins in the periphery of the focal spot were switched off using a 488 nm doughnut-shaped beam.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the imaging protocol.

claim: The 2D-doughnut was realized by using a phase plate, whereas the 3D-doughnut was generated by using a spatial light modulator.
source: The 2D-doughnut was realized by using a phase plate, whereas the 3D-doughnut was generated by using a spatial light modulator.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the technical implementation.

claim: On-state fluorophores at the center of the spot were read out with a Gaussian shaped beam of 488 nm light.
source: Third, on-state fluorophores at the center of the spot were read out with a Gaussian shaped beam of 488 nm light.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the imaging protocol.

claim: A short 5 µs break was introduced between each step of the switching scheme.
source: We introduced a short 5 µs break between each step.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the imaging protocol.

claim: The RESOLFT images were recorded with or without line accumulation depending on the signal intensity.
